reason: The text depicts a hierarchical leadership structure rather than genuine collaboration. Moses receives instructions from God and conveys them to the people (וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ כִּדְבַר־מֹשֶׁה), and the Israelites obey these directives (וּבְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל עָשׂוּ כִּדְבַר מֹשֶׁה). While both leaders and people work toward the common goal of the Exodus, the text shows command-and-obedience rather than mutual collaboration, with no evidence of the people proposing ideas, debating alternatives, or contributing their own strategic input. The people's role is responsive compliance to leadership directives.
